chunks: Present to them the example of the life of this world so like the water We send down from the skies that mingles with the earth to nourish its vegetation, which then on the morrow turns to stubble and is blown away by the wind. God has power over everything.
ai.seo_question: What is the metaphor of worldly life in Surah Al-Kahf?
ai.summary: This verse, often cited in Shia tafsir as a comprehensive metaphor for dunya, illustrates how divine decree causes worldly attractions to flourish briefly before withering into insignificance. It underscores the transient nature of material pursuits, reminding believers that just as rain nourishes plants only to be scattered by the wind, so too are earthly gains fleeting under God's absolute power.
